transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... yeah, um, I came in because I just... I can’t make myself go near the front windows at work anymore. Or even walk down that part of the street to get there. I keep finding excuses to stay in the back room, even though being out on the floor is, like, my whole job. 

I work retail, and my manager, Jessica, she's been getting kind of annoyed with me. Though honestly, she gets annoyed at everything. Like last week, we got this massive shipment of fall inventory and she made me spend four hours just unpacking these scented candles that nobody even buys. They smell awful, like fake pine needles and too much cinnamon? It gives me a headache just thinking about it, and the boxes were stacked practically to the ceiling. I had to break down so much cardboard. 

But yeah, anyway... I'm supposed to be up front greeting people, and I just... I keep hiding in the back because I can't go near the glass right now.

When you think about going near the front windows, does it bring on any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath, or are you mainly worried about having a panic attack in that area?

Um, no, not really? Like, my heart doesn't race and I don't get sweaty or feel like I can't breathe. And I'm not worried about having a panic attack or anything like that. I just... I just don't want to be near them. 

They're these massive floor-to-ceiling windows, right? And keeping them clean is practically impossible. Jessica actually made me use this really cheap glass cleaner a few weeks ago that left streaks absolutely everywhere, and then she had the nerve to blame me for it! Like, it's not my fault corporate won't buy actual Windex. They cut our store's supply budget by, like, half this year. We don't even have good paper towels in the employee bathroom anymore, just those awful thin brown ones that rip the second you try to pull them out of the dispenser, and they feel like sandpaper on your hands... 

But, um, wait, what were you asking? Oh, right. Yeah, no, my breathing is fine. I just can't go up there right now.
Is there something specific about the front windows or being near them that you find uncomfortable, or is it more of a general feeling that you just don’t want to be in that area?

Um, well, it's... it's because of the crash. Like, it just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. Especially when I'm trying to set up displays near the front, suddenly I can hear this huge bang and see the glass coming down like it's happening all over again. It's so loud in my head. 

And, you know, setting up those displays is already such a nightmare. Corporate sends down these planograms, right? And they expect us to follow them exactly, down to the inch, but our store layout is completely different from the flagship store they base the pictures on. So I'm always having to improvise, and then Jessica gets mad because the mannequin isn't angled exactly 45 degrees toward the door. As if anyone walking past the store actually cares about the exact angle of a plastic arm holding a faux-leather handbag. Which, by the way, those handbags are so overpriced this season. The stitching is terrible. I had a customer return one yesterday because the strap literally snapped off while she was putting her keys in it. And of course, she yelled at me like I personally sewed the thing... 

But yeah, I just... I see the glass shattering and I hear that noise, and I just can't be up there.
When you think about the crash and the glass shattering, does it feel like you're actually reliving the moment, or is it more like a memory popping into your head that you can easily dismiss?

Um, it's... I don't know if I'd say I'm reliving it exactly, but it's definitely not something I can just dismiss. It's more like... it just takes over for a second. Like I'm right back there, and then I'm not. 

But honestly, half the time my brain is just jumping all over the place anyway. Especially lately. I haven't been sleeping well at all. My apartment building has these incredibly thin walls, and my upstairs neighbor, I swear to God, he must be practicing tap dancing or something at 2:00 AM. It's just this constant *thud, thud, thud*. I've left three notes on his door, very politely asking him to keep it down, and he completely ignores them. And my landlord is totally useless. He's this guy named Gary who always wears socks with sandals, even in winter, and he just tells me to "buy earplugs." Like, I pay way too much rent for this place, I shouldn't have to sleep with foam shoved in my ears. Plus, the earplugs always fall out in the middle of the night anyway, and then I wake up to the stomping all over again...

But, um, what did you ask? Oh, right. Yeah, the memory. It's just really strong when it happens. I can't just shake it off.
When you think about the crash and the glass breaking, how does it make you feel emotionally? Do you feel scared, angry, or sad, or is it more like just a neutral memory?

Um, emotionally? I guess... I guess it just makes me feel really, really scared. Like this cold panic just washes over me. Definitely not neutral. It's just terrifying. 

Which is weird, because usually I'm not a scared person, you know? Like, I'm the one who deals with all the creepy bugs in the apartment because my roommate, Sarah, is absolutely terrified of spiders. Last week, there was this massive wolf spider in the bathtub. I swear it was the size of a Buick. And she was standing on the toilet seat, literally screaming, while I had to coax it into a Tupperware container. Which, by the way, she made me throw away the container afterward. It was one of the good ones, too, the glass kind with the snap-on lids that don't leak when you put soup in them. I bought a whole set at Target when they were on clearance, and now I'm missing the medium-sized square one, which is the most useful size for leftovers. It's so annoying because now I have to use the huge one for just a little bit of pasta, and it takes up way too much room in the fridge. Our fridge is tiny anyway, and Sarah always buys these giant jugs of iced coffee that take up the whole top shelf...

But, um, yeah. Scared. The memory just makes me feel really scared.
Do you ever feel like you’re actually experiencing the crash again, like it’s happening in real time, or do you just remember it happening?

Um, I think I already said this, but it's... it's like it's happening right then. Out of nowhere. Like, I'll just be trying to set up a display, and suddenly I hear that awful bang and see the glass falling. It's so real, it's not just remembering it. 

Which, honestly, setting up those displays is hard enough without having a panic attack in the middle of it. We got a new shipment of fall sweaters yesterday, and they're all these really scratchy, weird mustard colors. I don't know who is picking the colors for this season, but it's like they want everyone to look sick. And my manager, Dave, he insists that we fold them a very specific way, with this little cardboard insert so they stand up perfectly straight. But the cardboard pieces are always disappearing. I think the night crew throws them away because they don't want to deal with them. The night crew gets away with everything, I swear. They leave half-empty energy drinks on the registers, and then I'm the one who gets in trouble when the morning manager finds them. It's like, do I look like someone who drinks Monster Energy at 7:00 AM? I drink green tea. My mom got me this really nice loose-leaf tea for my birthday, but my tea infuser broke, the little chain just snapped right off...

But yeah, the crash. It feels like it's happening all over again. I can hear it and see the glass and everything.
When you experience the memory of the crash and the glass breaking, do you feel like you are actually back in that moment, as if the event is happening again right now?

Um, yeah... I think we just talked about this, right? Like, I told you it feels like it's happening right then. I hear the bang, I see the glass... it's like I'm right back in it. 

It's really frustrating because it's so distracting. Like I said, I'll just be at work, trying to deal with those awful mustard sweaters, and boom, I'm back in the crash. And honestly, it makes me feel like I can't even focus on the simplest things anymore. Like yesterday, I was supposed to be doing the window display, and I just completely zoned out. My coworker, Jessica, had to snap her fingers in front of my face. Jessica is... well, she's nice, but she wears this perfume that smells exactly like artificial grape flavoring. It is so overpowering. I don't know how she doesn't get a headache from it. I get a headache just standing next to her at the register. And she talks really loudly, too, especially when she's on her phone in the breakroom. She's always arguing with her boyfriend about his car. He has this old Honda Civic that he's constantly trying to fix up, but it just sits in their driveway leaking oil. My dad used to have a Honda, but it was a CR-V, one of the really old boxy ones, and it ran forever until...

Sorry, what was the question again? Did I answer it? Yeah, the crash feels like it's happening right now when it hits me.
Since the crash, have you found yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or unusually irritable, even when you're not near the front windows?

Um, yeah, definitely. I'm just constantly jumping at everything now. Like, if a delivery cart bangs in the back room, or if a car honks outside, or even if someone just comes up behind me without saying anything, I jump so hard my whole body jerks. And then my heart just keeps racing afterward, like it takes forever to calm down. 

Especially with the delivery carts. Gary, the guy who does receiving for our store, he uses this one heavy metal cart that squeaks and bangs over every single floor tile. I swear he never greases the wheels. I even told him once, like, Gary, WD-40 is literally four dollars at the hardware store next door. But he just laughed. He’s been working at the mall for like fifteen years and acts like he owns the place. He always takes the best parking spots, too, the ones under those big oak trees near the food court entrance so your car doesn't get boiling hot by the end of your shift. I had to park way out in the sun yesterday and my steering wheel literally burned my hands when I got in. I really need to buy one of those steering wheel covers, maybe one of the fuzzy ones? Though my friend Chloe had a pink fuzzy one and she said it shed all over her black leggings, which would be a disaster for me because our store dress code is all black. Black pants, black shoes... they are so strict about it. If you wear navy blue by accident, Dave will literally send you home to change.

But, um... yeah. I'm just really jumpy. A honk or a bang and my body just jerks and my heart goes crazy.
Since the crash, have you found yourself avoiding any other places or situations that remind you of what happened, even if they aren’t directly related to the front windows at work?

Um, yeah, I really try to avoid... well, I mean, I actually came in because I just can't make myself go near the front windows anymore. Or even that part of the street outside. I just can't do it. I keep finding all these excuses to stay in the back room, like offering to organize the stock or do the inventory counts, even though working the floor is supposed to be, like, my main job. 

Which, honestly, the back room is a disaster right now anyway. Corporate sent us all these holiday promotional materials way too early. Like, it's barely fall and we have boxes of fake snow and these giant cardboard reindeer taking up all the space. I don't know why retail always pushes the holidays so fast. It's like you can't even enjoy Halloween before they're shoving Christmas music down your throat. Last year, they started playing the holiday playlist on November 1st, and it only had like twelve songs on it. Do you know what it does to a person to hear Mariah Carey five times a shift? It's psychological torture. I actually complained to Dave about it, but he just said it's controlled by corporate and there's nothing he can do. Dave is so useless sometimes. He just sits in the back office eating those little bags of baby carrots and pretending to do the schedule. He always messes up my schedule, too. Like, I asked for Tuesdays off because my sister has her physical therapy appointments and I have to drive her, but he keeps putting me on the Tuesday morning shift... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, avoiding things. Yeah, I just stay away from the windows and the street. I stay in the back as much as I can.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you feel negative emotions like fear, anger, or guilt most of the time, even when you're not thinking about the event?

Um, no... not really. I mean, I don't think I feel angry or guilty all the time. I'm just mostly jumpy and, you know, trying to avoid the front of the store. But I don't walk around feeling mad at the world or anything like that. 

Although, I guess I do get a little annoyed sometimes, but that's just normal stuff. Like with my roommate, Sarah. She has this habit of leaving her wet towels on the bathroom floor, and it drives me absolutely crazy. I've asked her like a million times to just hang them up. We even bought this over-the-door rack specifically for towels, but she just tosses them on the tile. And then they get all musty smelling, and the whole bathroom smells like a damp basement. It's so gross. I ended up having to buy this expensive lavender room spray from Bath & Body Works just to mask the smell. I love their stuff, actually. They had this huge semi-annual sale last week and I bought like six candles. The Mahogany Teakwood one is my favorite, it smells exactly like Abercrombie & Fitch used to smell when I was in middle school. Did you ever go in there? It was always so dark you couldn't even see the clothes, and the music was so loud you had to scream at your friends. My mom hated taking me there...

But anyway, no, I don't think I have those negative feelings all the time. Just the normal amount, I guess.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you feel negative emotions like fear, anger, or guilt most of the time, even when you're not thinking about the event?

Um, wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? Yeah, I still don't think I'm walking around feeling angry or guilty all the time. Just the jumpiness and not wanting to be near the windows. 

Like I was saying about Sarah and the towels, that's just normal roommate stuff, you know? It's not like I'm having a breakdown over it. Though honestly, living with her is getting kind of exhausting. She started this new diet where she only eats things that are, like, raw or fermented? So our fridge is just full of these weird jars of kombucha and kimchi that smell so strong. Every time I open the door to get my coffee creamer, it's just this wave of cabbage smell. And I need my coffee. I have this special vanilla caramel creamer that I get from Target, and it's the only thing that gets me out of bed for those early shifts. Target has the best grocery section now, don't you think? I went in there yesterday just to buy toothpaste and ended up spending like eighty dollars on throw pillows and a new bath mat. They just suck you in with the home decor. I got this really cute yellow pillow that looks like a sunflower...

But yeah, to answer your question again, no, I don't feel bad or angry all the time. Just the normal stuff.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you feel negative emotions like fear, anger, or guilt most of the time, even when you're not thinking about the event?

Wait, are you asking me this again? I feel like we're stuck on a loop here. I really don't have this constant fear or anger or whatever. I'm just avoiding the front of the store, like I said. 

I mean, if anyone should be angry, it's my sister. She's the one dealing with all those physical therapy appointments I have to drive her to. They have her doing these weird exercises with resistance bands, and the physical therapist is this guy named Todd who always wears these really tight polo shirts. Like, uncomfortably tight. I don't know how he even moves his arms to show her the stretches. He reminds me of this guy I dated in high school, Jason. Jason was obsessed with going to the gym and drinking those massive protein shakes that smelled like chalk and artificial chocolate. He tried to get me to drink one once, and I swear I couldn't get the taste out of my mouth for two days. I had to eat an entire bag of Sour Patch Kids just to neutralize it. Sour candy is my absolute weakness. Whenever I go to the movies, I have to get a giant box of them, even though they cost like eight dollars now. Movie theater prices are just ridiculous these days, right? You spend fifty bucks just for a ticket and some snacks...

But honestly, no, I'm not walking around feeling guilty or scared all the time. I really think I've answered this one already.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you feel a persistent sense of fear, anger, or guilt, even when you're not reminded of the event or having a flashback?

Okay, seriously, is there a glitch happening? Because I'm pretty sure you just asked me the exact same thing again. Like, almost word for word. And my answer is still no, I don't have this constant dark cloud of fear or guilt or whatever hanging over me all day. 

Honestly, the only thing I'm persistently angry about right now is my stupid phone battery. It keeps dying when it says it's at like thirty percent. I took it to the Apple Store at the mall yesterday—well, not the mall where I work, a different one—and the guy at the Genius Bar was completely useless. He told me I had too many apps running in the background. Like, excuse me, I need my apps. How else am I supposed to keep up with TikTok? My For You page is literally perfect right now. It's all these videos of golden retrievers doing agility courses, and this one girl who does these insane makeup transformations where she turns herself into a literal Bratz doll. Have you seen those? It takes her like eight hours to paint her face. I don't know who has that kind of time. When I do my makeup for my shifts, it takes me exactly twelve minutes. Foundation, mascara, lip gloss, out the door. My manager is super strict about us wearing the company-approved lip colors anyway, which is so annoying because they only have these weird frosty pinks that completely wash me out... 

But yeah, no. No constant fear or guilt. I promise I'm not hiding anything, I just really don't feel like that.
Since the crash, have you found yourself feeling numb or detached from the things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, social activities, or even work?

Numb? No, I wouldn't say I feel numb or anything like that. I'm still doing all my normal stuff. Well, mostly. I mean, I still go to work, even though I'm trying to avoid that one section of the store right now. 

But I still like hanging out with my friends and everything. Actually, me and Sarah—my roommate, the one with the kombucha—we were supposed to go to this pottery painting place last weekend. It's one of those places where you pick a mug or a plate and just paint it, and then they fire it for you? I really wanted to paint this little ring dish to look like a watermelon. I saw it on Pinterest and thought it was so cute. I have this whole board dedicated to just watermelon-themed stuff. It started last summer when I bought this amazing watermelon-scented body scrub from Bath & Body Works. Oh my gosh, it smelled exactly like a Jolly Rancher. I used it so much I ran out in like a month, and when I went back to get more, they had already switched to their fall scents. Like, it was August, and they were already pushing pumpkin spice everything. It drives me crazy how stores rush the seasons. We're already putting out Christmas displays at my store, and it's barely even cold outside yet. I had to unpack like four boxes of these glittery reindeer ornaments yesterday, and the glitter got absolutely everywhere. It's in my hair, it's on my phone case... I swear I'm going to be finding red glitter in my apartment until next July. 

But yeah, I still enjoy things. I just haven't had a chance to do the pottery thing yet because of my sister's appointments and work and everything. So no, not numb.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you're unable to feel happy or experience joy, even during activities you usually enjoy?

No, I can still feel happy. I mean, I'm definitely stressed with everything going on, but I wouldn't say I've lost the ability to feel joy or anything dramatic like that. 

Like, I was definitely happy when my sister's physical therapist—the one with the tight shirts, Todd—finally said she could start putting a little more weight on her leg. We went through the drive-thru at Taco Bell to celebrate because she was craving a Crunchwrap Supreme. I swear, Taco Bell hits different when you haven't had it in a while. I always get the Cheesy Gordita Crunch, but I ask them to swap the regular taco shell inside for a Doritos Locos one. It's a game-changer, honestly. My friend Mark showed me that hack. Mark used to work there in high school, and he knew all the secret menu stuff. He actually got fired because he kept taking home entire boxes of the cinnamon twists at the end of his shift. Which, honestly, I get it, they're basically just air and sugar, but they're so addictive. He works at a car dealership now, which is so weird because he knows literally nothing about cars. He tried to tell me my brake pads were wearing out just by looking at my tires once, and I was like, Mark, you don't even know how to change your own oil. I always take my car to this place near my apartment because they have a shop cat named Barnaby who just sleeps on the counter all day. He's this massive orange tabby, and if you scratch him right behind the ears, he purrs so loud it sounds like an engine. 

But yeah, I still feel happy when good things happen, like seeing Barnaby or getting Taco Bell. I'm not, like, completely incapable of joy.
Since the crash, have you noticed that you have a hard time feeling positive emotions, like happiness or satisfaction, even when good things happen?

Okay, wait. Are you messing with me? Because I literally just answered this. Like, two seconds ago. It's the exact same question about feeling happy or positive emotions. Is this a test? Do you have to ask it a certain number of times for insurance purposes or something? 

Because my answer is still no. I don't have a hard time feeling happy. I just told you about the Taco Bell and Barnaby the cat. I'm fine with positive emotions. 

Honestly, the only thing I'm having a hard time with right now is figuring out what to wear to my cousin's wedding next month. It's supposed to be this whole fancy outdoor thing, but she picked the weirdest dress code. She called it "Rustic Glamour," which makes zero sense. Like, am I supposed to wear sequins with cowboy boots? Because I am not doing that. I tried on this one dress at Macy's that was kind of a dusty rose color, but it had these weird ruffled sleeves that made me look like a linebacker. My mom said it was "vintage," but my mom also thinks it's a good idea to put raisins in potato salad, so her judgment is highly questionable. I swear, every family barbecue, she brings that potato salad, and everyone just politely scoops it onto their plate and then pushes it around so it looks like they ate it. My uncle Dave actually fed his to the neighbor's dog once when he thought nobody was looking. The dog threw up on the patio later, which was a whole dramatic thing because it ruined my aunt's new outdoor rug. She had just bought it from Target, and she was so mad. Target has really good outdoor stuff right now, though. I bought these little solar-powered string lights for my balcony, and they look so cute at night. 

But anyway, no. I still feel happy and satisfied and all that. I'm just stressed about the wedding outfit. And the crash, obviously. But I can still feel good things.
Since the crash, have you noticed a loss of interest in things you used to care about, or feeling distant from people even when you're around them?

No, I haven't really lost interest in anything. I mean, I still care about all the stuff I usually care about. And I don't feel distant from people. I'm around people all the time, especially at work. 

Actually, speaking of being around people, my manager, Brenda, she's been scheduling me for all these closing shifts lately, and it's exhausting because the store is always a disaster by the end of the night. People just pick things up and put them down wherever they want. Like yesterday, I found a half-eaten soft pretzel tucked behind a display of throw pillows. Who does that? It's so gross. And the pillows were those really expensive velvet ones, too. I love velvet, but it is a magnet for dust and pet hair. I bought this velvet armchair off Facebook Marketplace a few months ago—it's this gorgeous emerald green—but I have to use a lint roller on it almost every single day because my roommate's cat just claims it as his personal throne. His name is Sir Pounce, which is ridiculous because he's like fifteen pounds and never pounces on anything. He mostly just lays there and judges you. I tried to put him on a diet, but my roommate keeps sneaking him those little squeeze tube treats. They smell absolutely awful, like low tide, but he goes crazy for them. 

But yeah, I still care about things. I care about my velvet chair, I care about my sister, I still like hanging out with my friends. I don't feel distant or anything.

The dog threw up on the patio later, which was a whole dramatic thing because it ruined my aunt's new outdoor rug. She had just bought it from Target, and she was so mad. Target has really good outdoor stuff right now, though. I bought these little solar-powered string lights for my balcony, and they look so cute at night. 

But anyway, no. I still feel happy and satisfied and all that. I'm just stressed about the wedding outfit. And the crash, obviously. But I can still feel good things.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences persistent negative alterations in mood related to PTSD, such as persistent negative emotional state, diminished interest in activities, or feelings of detachment, which would support F43.11 or F43.12 over F43.10.
doctor.question: Since the crash, have you noticed a loss of interest in things you used to care about, or feeling distant from people even when you're around them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest in activities or feeling detached/estranged from others, which are not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I haven't really lost interest in anything. I mean, I still care about all the stuff I usually care about. And I don't feel distant from people. I'm around people all the time, especially at work. 

Actually, speaking of being around people, my manager, Brenda, she's been scheduling me for all these closing shifts lately, and it's exhausting because the store is always a disaster by the end of the night. People just pick things up and put them down wherever they want. Like yesterday, I found a half-eaten soft pretzel tucked behind a display of throw pillows. Who does that? It's so gross. And the pillows were those really expensive velvet ones, too. I love velvet, but it is a magnet for dust and pet hair. I bought this velvet armchair off Facebook Marketplace a few months ago—it's this gorgeous emerald green—but I have to use a lint roller on it almost every single day because my roommate's cat just claims it as his personal throne. His name is Sir Pounce, which is ridiculous because he's like fifteen pounds and never pounces on anything. He mostly just lays there and judges you. I tried to put him on a diet, but my roommate keeps sneaking him those little squeeze tube treats. They smell absolutely awful, like low tide, but he goes crazy for them. 

But yeah, I still care about things. I care about my velvet chair, I care about my sister, I still like hanging out with my friends. I don't feel distant or anything.

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and ask for the primary reason for their visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent intrusive memories and flashbacks of a traumatic event (car crash involving breaking glass), marked avoidance of stimuli associated with the trauma (front windows at work and adjacent street), and persistent increased reactivity (e.g., being easily startled). These symptoms align with PTSD, chronic. The absence of persistent negative emotional states and detachment supports against a more complex or prolonged stress disorder.
